title: Part 1
text: Could you simply cook the meat to make it safe? Here is the most unsettling part of the whole story.

title: Part 2
text: With most dangerous germs, cooking works. Salmonella and E. coli are destroyed when heat unravels their proteins. A good kitchen is usually enough.
nxt: So you might expect the same for the infection behind kuru.

title: Part 3
text: But prions are different. Normal cooking does not reliably inactivate them. They can survive the chemicals used to preserve tissue, such as formaldehyde.
nxt: And a standard hospital sterilizing cycle is not enough, which is why hospitals use harsher protocols after surgery on a patient with a prion disease.

title: Part 4
text: How tough are they? In a laboratory study published in the year 2000, a team led by Paul Brown heated infected hamster brain to six hundred degrees Celsius.
nxt: A small amount of infectivity still survived. It did not survive at one thousand degrees. That was one experiment on one strain, but it shows how stubborn prions can be.

title: Part 5
text: Now think about your immune system. It usually spots invaders by the foreign proteins on their surface. But a prion is built from a protein your own body makes.
nxt: So there is no useful defense. No antibody response. No fever. No early warning.

title: Part 6
text: And it can wait. Kuru has one of the longest incubation periods ever recorded.
nxt: A study of the last patients found that some fell ill about forty years after exposure, and the researchers concluded that the delay could exceed fifty years.

title: Part 7
text: There is a related story from Britain. In the 1980s and 1990s, cattle were fed meat-and-bone meal made from the remains of other animals, and a prion disease spread through the herds.
nxt: It was called mad cow disease. In 1996, a human form linked to it was reported. The lesson was clear: feeding animals to their own species is dangerous.

title: Part 8
text: To be accurate, eating a person is not automatically a prion infection. The risk exists when that person had a prion disease.
nxt: But the danger is invisible, and the delay is so long that no one could tell in time.

title: Part 9
text: Nature's message was clear: do not recycle your own species through the food chain. The full video explains why.
